extracted.intended_audience: writers submitting short speculative fiction to Strange Horizons
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for authors submitting short speculative-fiction stories to the magazine Strange Horizons, covering eligibility, length, format, rights, payment, and editorial preferences. Intended to help prospective contributors prepare and submit work correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: We want: Speculative fiction, broadly defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your story doesn't have a speculative element, or strong speculative-fiction sensibilities, it's probably not for us.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word-count limits and preferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Up to 10,000 words (under 5000 preferred).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We prefer stories under 5,000 words, but consider up to 10,000 words. The longer the story is, the less likely we are to be interested. Our wordcount limit is not absolutely inflexible, but we can't consider stories much over the limit, not even as serials. We have no minimum wordcount requirement; we consider short-short stories. We determine story length by taking the word-processor wordcount and rounding up to the next highest 100 words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission method (required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitted here, via our Moksha submissions system — no email or postal submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In order to track stories correctly, we can only consider stories submitted through that form—no email or paper mail submissions. If you haven't received an autoresponse within 24 hours, query immediately (missing autoresponse usually means we have an incorrect email address for you).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted file formats and manuscript formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Please send only RTF, DOC or DOCX files and try to stick to standard manuscript format as much as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Along with your name and contact information in the upper left, you may also add your pronouns (optional). If you're having trouble submitting, email fiction@strangehorizons.com with subject 'QUERY: Your Question Topic'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required author identification on manuscript
rubrics_metrics.description: Include your name and contact information in the upper left; pronouns optional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This helps editors identify and contact authors; keep cover letter minimal and don't include plot synopses in the cover letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simultaneous and multiple submissions policy
rubrics_metrics.description: No simultaneous or multiple submissions; no re-submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions sent to us and another venue simultaneously are not allowed. Multiple stories at once from the same author are not allowed. If you withdraw a story, we won't consider any version of that story in the future (see withdrawal policy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission / previously-submitted-to-Strange-Horizons policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories previously submitted to Strange Horizons, even if they have been revised, will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not resubmit stories that have already been sent to Strange Horizons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Previously published in English / originality requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Previously unpublished in English — we buy first English rights, including audio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We will consider stories which have previously appeared in another language, but have never been published in English.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translations and Samovar (sister magazine)
rubrics_metrics.description: Special note on translations: our quarterly sister magazine Samovar specializes in translations: we encourage you to submit all translations there first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Samovar and Strange Horizons have independent submissions queues and different editors, and submissions to either magazine are only read for that magazine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment rates and terms
rubrics_metrics.description: We pay 10¢/word USD, with a minimum payment of $60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment is made within 60 days of contract; payment by check or PayPal according to the author's preference. SFWA officially considers Strange Horizons a professional market.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights purchased and duration
rubrics_metrics.description: We buy first-printing world exclusive English-language rights (including audio rights) for six (6) months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After that period, you are free to republish the story elsewhere. The editors hope to leave the story in the archives indefinitely after it's rotated off the main table of contents, but you have the right to remove your story from the archives at any time after one (1) year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial interests — diversity and perspective
rubrics_metrics.description: Fiction from or about diverse perspectives and traditionally under-represented groups, settings, and cultures, written from a non-exoticizing and well-researched position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The magazine particularly loves work that represents diverse voices responsibly; exoticizing or superficial portrayals are discouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial interests — style and structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Unusual yet readable styles and inventive structures and narratives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experimental approaches that remain readable are welcomed; the editors note an interest in inventive storytelling techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial interests — political complexity
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories that address political issues in complex and nuanced ways, resisting oversimplification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work that treats political themes with subtlety and depth is of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental and interactive fiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Hypertext fiction, interactive fiction, and other stories that explore and exploit the forms available to us.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have a work of this type that you think might be a good fit for Strange Horizons, please query us to discuss how to submit it (i.e., ask editors about submission method).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable content: profanity, sex, and violence
rubrics_metrics.description: Profanity is fine. Sex or violence in a story should be artistically justified; no excessive gore.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use whatever words are appropriate for your story; explicit content should serve the art rather than be gratuitous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic and spelling flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: We welcome submissions from anywhere in the world, and British spellings are fine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The magazine is open to international submissions and variant English spellings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms not accepted by the fiction department
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry or nonfiction; we're the wrong department for those.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit poetry or nonfiction to the appropriate department or venue rather than the fiction submissions system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unacceptable story types
rubrics_metrics.description: Things we won't consider: Stories above 10,000 words, including serialized novels or novellas; partial or incomplete stories; unsolicited reprints of works previously published in English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not send partial/incomplete work or reprints previously published in English; serials and novellas exceed the magazine's scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover letter guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Your cover letter can be minimal: generally, these should be short and list just a few of your most recent or most relevant publications or workshops.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have life experience relevant to your story (e.g., your story takes place on a submarine and you served on a submarine), mention that. Cover letters shouldn't include plot synopses or pitches. See the sample cover letters page for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response and autoresponder policy
rubrics_metrics.description: We send an autoresponder message in response to every submission we receive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you haven't received an autoresponse within 24 hours after submitting, please query immediately (missing an autoresponse usually means we have an incorrect email address for you). Please query if you're concerned your submission has gone astray.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal policy
rubrics_metrics.description: After you submit a story, we strongly prefer you don't withdraw it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you withdraw a story, we won't consider any version of that story in the future. If you do need to withdraw a story, send an e-mail telling us that you need to withdraw, and let us know why.
